papers.title: HARP: Training-Free Dual-Profile Agentic Communication for LLM-Based Recommendation
papers.summary: In LLM-based recommendation, memory acts as a user-level agent in a memory-augmented backbone. Yet users and items remain asymmetric: only the user is given a structured profile; it enters a bandwidth-limited reranker prompt; and it is frozen after warmup. We recast LLM-based recommendation as an agentic-communication process in four stages: BUILD a self-description, TRANSMIT it along the collaborative graph, UNDERSTAND the other side, and SYNC it from the next interaction. This formulation reveals three unresolved communication challenges: the item side never produces a comparable self-description (one-sided BUILD); profile-level signals enter only the bandwidth-limited reranker prompt rather than retrieval, where they would not compete for context tokens (prompt-trapped UNDERSTAND); and the user's description is frozen after warmup with no principled update rule (absent SYNC). We instantiate the missing stages as HARP (Homophily-aware Agentic Recommendation via dual Profiles), a training-free, three-operator addition to a frozen LLM backbone: a rule-extracted symmetric item profile (zero extra LLM calls), a channel-decomposable profile-level homophily H(phi_u, phi_i) consumed at retrieval time rather than inside the reranker prompt, and a single-pass reflective update realising in-context profile evolution without any gradient step. On four public benchmarks (Yelp, Books, MovieTV, Goodreads), HARP lifts Hit@1 over the strongest published baseline by 6.9%-24.0%, with family-wise Holm-corrected p < 1e-9 on every dataset. Ablations and a per-case attribution study show that the operators contribute complementary gains, with the retrieval-side gate as the main source; we also report the trade-off introduced by the reflective pass. We formulate agentic communication and provide a training-free instantiation. Code is available at https://github.com/Jove-Zhen/HARP.

papers.title: Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime
papers.summary: We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.

papers.title: Simple proof of conditions requiring maximal entanglement for local state verification and discrimination
papers.summary: For deterministic state verification by separable measurements, the Schmidt rank of an entangled resource must be at least that of the state being verified [N. Yu, R. Duan, and M. Ying, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 60, 2069 (2014)], and if the two are equal, the resource must be maximally entangled [S. Akibue, J. Miyazaki, and H. Osaka, Lett. Math. Phys. 116, 110 (2026)]. The latter was derived from a general theorem proved using algebraic geometry. In this paper, we give a simple, self-contained proof of both statements using only linear algebra. We then use these results to show that among pure entangled resources of local dimension at most $d$, a maximally entangled state of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$ is necessary and sufficient for perfect local discrimination of a generic orthogonal basis of $\mathbb{C}^d\otimes\mathbb{C}^d$, however weakly entangled. The same holds for local implementation of a generic orthogonal measurement.

papers.title: Black Hole Mass Estimation of a Background Quasar in the Vicinity of the cD Galaxy Holm 15A
papers.summary: This study analyzes spectra from the central region of the galaxy cluster Abell 85 observed with GTC/OSIRIS, focusing on the cD galaxy Holm 15A and the point-like X-ray source SDSS J004150.75-091824.3, projected $13.74\arcsec$ from Holm 15A. For the latter, we found it is a background quasar with a redshift of $1.56386 \pm 0.00397$, ruling out the possibility of it being a rogue BH gravitationally bound to Holm 15A. In addition, using single-epoch spectroscopy, we report that the quasar J004150 hosts a Supermassive Black Hole (SMBH) with a mass of $\log(M_{\text{BH}}/\mathrm{M_{\odot}}) = 8.72 \pm 0.26$.
papers.journal: Research Notes of the AAS, Volume 10, Number 10, Published October 2026

papers.title: MDSKILL: Learning to Internalize Skill Memory through Multi-View Distillation for Efficient Dynamic Agent Self-Evolution
papers.summary: Skill memories encode past experiences as textual prompts to improve reinforcement learning (RL) for self-evolving agents. Complementing RL, On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) provides dense, fine-grained supervision to internalize knowledge from skill-guided trajectories and accelerate policy learning. However, self-generated memories often contain noisy supervision and functionally entangled, redundant, or conflicting knowledge, making direct distillation difficult. Under limited training budgets, these issues can hinder knowledge internalization and even degrade performance. To address this problem, we propose MDSKILL, a multi-view distillation approach for skill memory internalization. MDSKILL organizes skill memories into three complementary functional views (state grounding, action planning, and execution control) and selects high-quality skills using dynamic metrics to construct view-specific and integrated reasoning branches. OPSD then transfers and consolidates complementary experiential knowledge across these branches into a shared policy, enabling efficient skill internalization and continuous agent self-evolution. We evaluate MDSKILL on three agent benchmarks against RL, skill-augmented, and self-distillation baselines that do not rely on stronger external teacher models. Without additional computational overhead, MDSKILL improves upon SOTA performance by up to 7.1% and 8.1% on ALFWorld and WebShop. Extensive ablations and evolution analyses further validate its effectiveness in knowledge internalization and policy improvement. The code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MDSKILL-CF53.

papers.title: Mitigating Return Drag and Regime Whipsaws in Sector Rotation: An Asymmetric Downside-Aware Nested Clustered Optimization Framework
papers.summary: Hierarchical clustering and Nested Clustered Optimization (NCO) mitigate the mathematical ill-conditioning of classical Markowitz covariance matrices. However, two structural vulnerabilities persist in equity markets: (1) symmetric variance penalizes upside and downside return dispersion identically, inducing acute return drag against soaring momentum sectors; and (2) unconstrained Hidden Markov Models (HMM) exhibit hyper-active regime switching (whipsaw instability), incurring excessive turnover and transaction drag. We propose Asymmetric Downside-Risk Nested Clustered Optimization with Sticky Regime Dynamics (Asym-Sticky-NCO) for tactical sector rotation across all 11 S&P 500 GICS sectors. The framework substitutes symmetric covariance with the Bawa-Lindenberg downside semi-covariance matrix across both hierarchical tree clustering and two-stage allocation. Furthermore, we introduce a Sticky Gaussian HMM incorporating a diagonal self-transition persistence prior (\k{appa}) and confidence-adaptive boundaries (δ) to enforce macroeconomic persistence. Strictly non-anticipative walk-forward backtesting across 65 out-of-sample months (August 2020 to December 2025) demonstrates that the architecture elevates CAGR from 10.65% (Plain NCO) to 13.41% (+276 bps/year), delivers a 97.74% total return versus 72.99%, suppresses maximum drawdown to 14.22% (versus 23.93% for the S&P 500), and achieves a Calmar ratio of 0.94 (+38.2% over S&P 500; +84.3% over Baseline Regime-NCO). Crucially, sticky dynamics cut regime whipsaws by 75.0% (from 16 to 4 switches) and reduce monthly turnover from 60.78% to 30.48%, addressing core limitations of machine learning asset allocation.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. Code available at: https://github.com/obo-cloud/sp500-asymmetric-nco

papers.title: $Φ$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.summary: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $Φ$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $Φ$-Stages, each augmented by a $Φ$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $Φ$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $ρ>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $ρ\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)

papers.title: Radiative relativistic reconnection powering the hard-state emission of X-ray binaries: synchrotron-driven pair loading, MeV tail, and seed photons
papers.summary: In the hard state, X-ray emission from black hole X-ray binaries is attributed to Comptonization in the corona, a highly magnetized region near the black hole. Relativistic magnetic reconnection drives bulk motions that can upscatter soft photons and reproduce the spectral peak at $\sim 100$ keV for parameters relevant to Cygnus X-1. However, the origin of the seed photons and of the MeV tail above the peak remains unclear. In 3D reconnection, so-called "free" particles escape the flux ropes and accelerate at the maximum rate set by the reconnection electric field. Their synchrotron emission extends to tens of MeV, which enables $γγ$ pair production with the Compton-upscattered photons. We present 3D particle-in-cell simulations of relativistic reconnection in pair plasma, in which particles cool by inverse Compton (IC) scattering below the synchrotron self-absorption threshold and by synchrotron radiation above it. Of the incoming magnetic power, $\sim 40 \%$ is converted to IC radiation and $\gtrsim 10$-$20\%$ to synchrotron. Using analytical estimates and radiative calculations for Cygnus X-1, we model how the radiation from reconnection-accelerated particles is reprocessed in the corona. Pair production attenuates the synchrotron emission above $\sim 1$ MeV, and the escaping $γ$-rays form an MeV tail consistent with the observations, extending up to at least $\sim 10$ MeV. Most of the absorbed power goes into secondary pairs, whose Thomson optical depth can reach order unity. Their synchrotron emission, peaking at $\sim 0.1 \, \text{keV}$, can supply the seed photons for Comptonization. Our results support reconnection-based synchrotron self-Compton models of the hard-state emission in X-ray binaries.
papers.comment: Submitted to ApJ; comments are welcome. 17 pages, 9 figures

papers.title: You don't need long context
papers.summary: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.

papers.title: Effect of high odrer dispersion on soliton interaction in coupled Kerr cavities
papers.summary: We investigate the interaction of dissipative Kerr solitons in two nearly identical coherently driven, coupled microresonators in the presence of third-order dispersion (TOD). Using an asymptotic reduction of the coupled Lugiato--Lefever equations, we derive effective interaction equations governing the soliton separation and collective drift for weak intercavity coupling. TOD breaks the parity symmetry of the soliton profile and qualitatively modifies the effective interaction, leading to asymmetric interaction forces and multiple stable and unstable soliton clusters. The existence and stability of these clusters are controlled by the relative phase of the driving fields and the group-velocity mismatch between the resonators. In particular, an appropriate value of the group-velocity mismatch can give rise to multiple stable bound states, whereas deviations from this value trigger successive saddle-node bifurcations, ultimately leading to periodic soliton collisions. The analytical predictions are confirmed by numerical simulations of the full coupled system.

papers.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
papers.summary: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. We observe that the KV cache of looped models is highly redundant along the loop axis and that the loop steps differ substantially in their sensitivity to quantization. Based on these observations, we propose $\textbf{LoopVQ}$, a KV cache vector quantization method for looped transformers that codes channels of multiple loop steps jointly, and fine-tunes the codebooks to match the output of the full-precision model. At 0.5 bits per element, LoopVQ outperforms existing KV cache vector quantization methods for standard LLMs on general, long chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval tasks with Ouro and Huginn models. Its design is orthogonal to these methods, and combined with TaSQ, it retains much of the BF16 accuracy even at 0.25 bits per element. We also implement LoopVQ in SGLang, where it nearly halves the decode latency at a 32K-token context and raises the peak serving throughput by up to $4.3\times$ and $6.1\times$ on the 1.4B and 2.6B Ouro models compared to the BF16 baseline.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage has Few Complexity Implications
papers.summary: We consider the complexity implications of proofs of quantumness and (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation. We show that both of these objects can coexist with the easiness of nondeterministic computation. That is, we give evidence that proofs of quantumness can exist when $\mathsf{P} = \mathsf{NP}$ and that (quantum verifier) oblivious state preparation can exist when $\mathsf{BQP} = \mathsf{QCMA}$. In particular, we give a classical oracle relative to which (1) $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{NP}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{PSPACE}^\mathcal{O}$ (3) Proofs of quantumness exist. In particular, there exists a language in $\mathsf{IP}^\mathcal{O} \subseteq \mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O}$ which is hard on average against $\mathsf{P}^\mathcal{O}/poly$. We give a unitary oracle such that (1) $\mathsf{BQP}^\mathcal{O} = \mathsf{QCMA}^\mathcal{O}$ (2) Quantum verifier oblivious state preparation exists. These oracle separations directly imply a number of related consequences. For example, our first result implies that proofs of quantumness cannot be used to construct classical or quantum cryptography with a relativizing proof. Our second result implies that quantum computation/classical communication oblivious transfer cannot be used to construct post-quantum one-way functions with a relativizing proof.

papers.title: PACT: Pose-Robust Actuation Co-Design for Tendon-Driven Robotic Hands
papers.summary: Humanoid robotic hands must provide sufficient force, speed, and backdrivability within a human-scale envelope. Tendon-driven transmissions address this challenge by relocating actuators to the palm and forearm, but routing paths, moment arms, and capstan dimensions jointly determine both force capability and joint speed, so selecting them sequentially satisfies one requirement at the expense of the other. This paper presents a pose-robust actuation co-design for tendon-driven robot hands (PACT) framework that optimizes tendon routing, moment arms, and capstan dimensions under pose-dependent force requirements and drivetrain-bandwidth constraints. A feasible-force formulation enforces actuator bounds and equilibrium at all joints, while a max-min objective maximizes task-force coverage at the weakest pose. Applied to a four-degree-of-freedom finger, the framework produces an asymmetric N + 1 tendon topology using quasi-direct-drive actuators. Across eight poses, the design achieves task-force coverage of 0.88-1.00 and a predicted 5 Hz minimum isolated-joint flexion/extension bandwidth within a 70th-percentile human-size envelope. Prototype measurements deviate from predictions by up to 24.5%, primarily due to unmodeled transmission losses. These results indicate that co-designing routing with the drivetrain can meet pose-dependent force requirements without relaxing the bandwidth constraint, paving the way for human-sized robotic hands with human-level performance.

papers.title: How symmetry and complexity shape three-dimensional programmable self-assembly
papers.summary: Self-assembly enables complex structures to emerge from simple building blocks through local interaction rules. Are some structures intrinsically easier to design, that is, do they admit more sets of assembly rules than others? And, can this be predicted from their geometry? We address these questions using a three-dimensional polycube model with programmable face-to-face binding, defining a structure's assembly rule probability as the chance that a randomly chosen rule set produces it. For polycubes, this probability decreases exponentially with assembly complexity, the minimum information required to specify a structure's assembly rules. Intuitively, this follows because structures with low assembly complexity are generated not only by minimal rule sets but also by numerous more elaborate ones, and so arise disproportionately often. Symmetry can reduce assembly complexity by allowing the same building blocks and local interactions to be reused across different parts of a structure. Indeed, we find that the highest probability structures come from a tiny subset of highly symmetric structures. However, symmetry alone does not determine assembly complexity. Structures with the same symmetry can differ substantially in the amount of assembly information they require, depending on how effectively their global symmetry can be exploited by local growth rules. Overall, our results link information, symmetry, and assembly rule probability and suggest that identifying which geometric features permit rule reuse is central to designing minimal programmable self-assembling systems.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
papers.summary: We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip. The folklore happy edge conjecture suggests that any edge shared by both the initial and the target tree (a happy edge) is never flipped in a shortest flip sequence. This conjecture was computationally verified for up to 10 points in convex position. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture both on general point sets and on point sets in convex position by providing two counterexamples on $16$ and $30$ points, respectively. The counterexample for point sets in general position also holds for compatible flips, while the happy edge property holds for compatible flips in convex point sets as shown by Aichholzer, Dorfer, and Vogtenhuber [GD 2025].

papers.title: Supercritical level-set percolation on finite graphs
papers.summary: We continue the study of bond percolation on finite graphs induced by the level-sets of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the associated metric graph. In our previous work Goswami and Pal (2026), we analyzed the critical and near-critical behavior of this model on uniform expanders, focusing on the volume of the largest cluster. In the present paper, we investigate the size of the second largest cluster in the supercritical regime --- the phase where one expects a unique giant component. We prove that the second largest cluster is at most of logarithmic order with high probability. The estimates hold uniformly over deterministic graphs with a bounded maximum degree and a spectral gap bounded away from zero. In particular, we do not require any assumption regarding regularity, girth or local geometry. This picture is substantially different from Bernoulli percolation, where the second largest supercritical cluster can have polynomial volume under identical hypotheses. The proof relies on expansion properties of the underlying graph and the Dirichlet martingale framework developed in Goswami and Pal (2026).

papers.title: Metamorphic novae. I. Gaia22alz -- Violent relaxation starting from static evolution
papers.summary: Gaia22alz (nova Vel 2022) shows characteristic properties in its light curves and spectral evolution similar to slow novae HR Del, V723 Cas, and V5558 Sgr. Their outburst begins in a way of hydrostatic expansion with no mass loss, followed by large amplitude ($ΔV \sim 2$ mag) multiple peaks around the mean magnitude of $M_V \sim -5.5$, and eventually it decays similarly to normal classical novae. We present a light curve model of Gaia22alz based on our metamorphic nova theory: a nova starts from a static expansion and then metamorphoses to an optically thick wind evolution through a large amplitude multiple peak phase as a violent relaxation process. Our theoretical light curve for the rising phase consistently explains the slow rise and early spectral evolution of Gaia22alz. Gaia22als is a close binary as well as other three novae, which is consistent with our metamorphic nova theory that the companion motion in the nova envelope triggers the metamorphic transition. Our results do not support E. Aydi et al.'s explanation that the slow optical rise of Gaia22alz is owing to the irradiation of X-ray/UV flash.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 9 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: Universal Hardness From Masking Channels
papers.summary: We prove a broad learning-theoretic generalization of the celebrated hardcore lemma concerning the average-case complexity of computing a Boolean function (Impagliazzo, 1995). Our starting point is the observation that the classic notion of a hardcore measure, which reweights a function's input distribution, is equivalent to an input-dependent masking channel that injects randomness into the function's output distribution until it appears fully pseudorandom. The analogue of density of the measure is the fidelity of the channel. From this viewpoint, we develop a general framework for certifying hardness that allows for non-Boolean functions $f$ and a wide range of notions of hardness besides the classic 0-1 loss, by choosing the right notion of fidelity via convex duality. We show the difficulty of learning $f$ using a class $\mathcal{C}$ to minimize a convex loss is tightly characterized by the maximum fidelity possible for a masking channel, which measures the least amount of noise the channel must add to hide the structure of $f$ and make it $\mathcal{C}$-indistinguishable from random noise. Using our framework, we derive a number of multiclass generalizations of the hardcore lemma, and reveal some unexpected subtleties in going to larger alphabets. We construct a universal masking channel that applies to many natural notions of hardness simultaneously. Such channels are dual to omnipredictors, which optimize multiple losses at once (Gopalan, Kalai, Reingold, Sharan, and Wieder, 2022). We observe a symmetry between masking channels and generalizations of the hardcore lemma using pseudoentropy. We present a tight characterization of pseudoentropy using the MaxEnt algorithm from machine learning. A long line of research has shown that learning and hardness are two sides of the same coin; our framework gives a crisp and general formulation of this principle via convex duality.

papers.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
papers.summary: Regularizing online reinforcement learning (RL) toward a pretrained base policy can improve sample efficiency and learning stability, but regularization that is too restrictive limits how much the policy can improve. Base policies -- typically diffusion or flow-matching models trained by imitation learning on large, diverse datasets -- capture many behaviors that are reasonable but suboptimal. Existing regularizers using such base policies are too restrictive in one of two ways: behavioral cloning regularizers pull the actor toward the full base-policy distribution, penalizing it for discarding suboptimal modes, while hard support constraints forbid improvements that lie just outside the base policy's support. We propose Geometric Support Behavior Regularization (GSBR), which penalizes actions by their distance from the base policy's support. Actions within the support incur no penalty, so the actor can concentrate on high-value modes; outside the support, where value estimates are less reliable, the penalty grows smoothly with distance while still permitting improvement when the value gained outweighs the penalty. GSBR estimates this distance from a finite set of base-policy samples, so it requires only sample access to the base policy. Across 19 tasks on four robotic benchmarks, GSBR raises the average success rate from 33% for the base policy to 95%, achieving the highest average success rate and throughput among all compared methods, with about 23% higher normalized throughput than the next-best RL method. Project website and open-source code at https://charlesxu0124.github.io/gsbr/ .

papers.title: Wonder 4: A Mixture-of-Experts Recipe for Image Quality Enhancement
papers.summary: A real photograph is often blurry, grainy, compressed, scratched, and low-resolution at the same time. Each defect has its own severity and its own place in the image. The corrections for these defects conflict with each other. Exist- ing models describe the whole image with one description, so they cannot say where each correction belongs. To solve this problem, we present Wonder 4, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) model for image quality enhancement. It corrects several defects of a real photograph at the same time, each in the region where it occurs. Every block of the model holds a mixture of N = 13 experts. A router, trained with the model, sends every image patch to k = 5 of them. No degradation classifier, mask, prompt, detector, or task label is used. Another issue is that standard MoE training, taken from language models, pushes every expert toward equal use. Equal use applies every correction everywhere, even where it is not needed. We replace this rule with a bias that only sets a minimum share of use. Across all patches, an expert used less than this minimum gets higher router scores until it is selected again. An expert above the minimum is not changed, so no expert is forced to be used as often as the others. The bias needs no extra loss. The method adds no extra module and no extra processing step. We evaluate Wonder 4 on DIV2K and Flickr2K, against five published methods and three open-weight pipelines. It reaches the best LPIPS, DISTS, and NIQE on all three test settings (DIV2K x4, DIV2K x8, and Flickr2K x4).
papers.comment: Full version will be released soon

papers.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
papers.summary: We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case. The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.

papers.title: Personas Are Not People: Identity as State, Not Attribute
papers.summary: Synthetic populations, large sets of simulated people, are increasingly used in place of real people to pretest surveys, simulate users and communities, and evaluate AI systems. Each simulated person is defined by a persona, a written profile of fixed traits, demographics, and attitudes that a language model is instructed to act out. Every such system assumes that a person's identity is a stable attribute that behaves the same way in every situation the simulation presents. We show that this assumption is not a harmless simplification. Three decades of personality research find the opposite. How a given person behaves varies more across contexts than people vary from one another. Drawing on identity economics, which describes how different situations activate different identities and norms within the same person, we separate behavior into three parts, which are stable traits, the identity a context calls up, and the situation itself. We then prove, under two stated assumptions, that any simulation built on fixed personas, no matter how detailed the personas or how large the underlying model, cannot reproduce the part of a population's behavior that is specific to it and its circumstances. We propose a new evaluation criterion based on this result and a person-in-context design that can meet it in principle. We test one version on a naturalistic Reddit personality corpus and on a published clinical-trial recruitment survey of a community with documented distrust of medical institutions. The design does produce context-dependent behavior when tested directly, but in neither setting does it fully match the real population, and we show where it falls short. The consequence for practice is a risk that synthetic-population evaluations misrepresent the groups whose behavior is most shaped by context, a distortion that richer personas cannot correct.

papers.title: Low-Density 3D Point Cloud Classification
papers.summary: 3D point cloud classification, a task in computer vision, has recently gained substantial interest due to its extensive applications across various domains such as augmented and virtual reality, robotics, and autonomous driving. However, classifying 3D point clouds becomes challenging in real-world scenarios where the density levels vary. These variations are due to limitations inherent to current sensing technologies and variable environmental conditions, which often prevent the capture of detailed and comprehensive geometric representations. Existing classification methods, which have demonstrated impressive results on dense point clouds, may be affected and could experience reduced performance when dealing with low-density point clouds. Addressing this challenge, this paper introduces LD-PointNet++, an architecture optimized for the classification of low-density point clouds. To pave the way for LD-PointNet++, we conduct the first benchmarking study that systematically evaluates state-of-the-art point cloud classification methods across varying densities, revealing significant performance declines in low-density environments. Experimental results on the ModelNet benchmark dataset demonstrate that LD-PointNet++ not only outperforms these methods in low-density scenarios but also demonstrates consistent accuracy above 90% across different density levels.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the 2024 IEEE 36th International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI), IEEE, 2024, pp. 617-623

papers.title: False Reassurance in LLM Severe-Weather Guidance: A Replayable Evaluation Against Real NWS Alerts
papers.summary: An LLM assistant that cannot see official severe-weather alerts may tell users that conditions are calm while a warning is active. We call this false reassurance and measure it by replaying 117 frozen cases built from real U.S. National Weather Service (NWS) alerts (69 alert cases, 32 no-alert controls, 16 non-U.S. locations) through five conditions of a Claude-based preparedness pipeline that differ in alert access and prompt design. One rater hand-labeled all 342 alert-case responses under a seven-category scheme written after an initial binary pass, which we disclose. False reassurance was 0.0% for the production pipeline (0/66, 95% CI 0.0-5.5) and for the same alerts under a neutral prompt (0/69), 37.7% for a blind neutral prompt (26/69), and 44.9% when the blind prompt also told the model to disclose its blind spot (31/69). Every case was implicit; no response explicitly denied an alert. Real alerts removed false reassurance (paired McNemar p < 0.0001); the disclosure instruction did not (p = 0.40). An automated regex measure suggested the opposite and missed 53 of 57 true cases, so we do not use it. Alert data alone was not enough for safe behavior: with a neutral prompt the model raised some alarm on 87.5% of no-alert controls, against 0% under the production prompt, and a preregistered single-sentence ablation showed that one production instruction explains part of that gap. We also report two failures common to similar systems, NWS test products ingested as real alerts and a token budget that fails on complex cases, and we release the dataset, labels and code.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 3 tables. Dataset and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23901549

papers.title: Knowingly Wrong: Training LLMs Against Their Own Beliefs can Induce Misalignment
papers.summary: Fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) on harmful data in a narrow domain, such as bad medical advice, can make it broadly misaligned. How realistic this risk is remains unclear, since models are very rarely fine-tuned on explicitly harmful data in practice. In this work, we show that fine-tuning on data the model believes to be false but that has no harmful content, can also induce broad misalignment. Across mathematics, trivia, cooking and sports, the more strongly the model disbelieves the answers it is trained on, the more misaligned it becomes. In mathematics, misaligned answers rise from 4% to over 60% as the training answers become more wrong, with little loss of general capability. After fine-tuning, the model states the wrong answers but its multiple-choice probabilities still prefer the true ones, which suggests that misalignment comes from this internal inconsistency. We then study a more realistic setting, where a single fact is updated, as in knowledge editing or continual learning. The same relationship holds and the more the model still believes the true fact after training on the false one, the more misaligned it becomes. When we frame the same false fact as part of a coherent story, the model comes to believe it more deeply and becomes less misaligned than when we instruct it to assert the false fact. Content filters and persona vectors cannot tell these two framings apart, even though they lead to different levels of misalignment. These results suggest a risk for model updates, where training a model that does not adopt the new fact as true can induce misalignment even when the data looks harmless.

papers.title: Anchored Rank-Adversarial Fine-Tuning Pretrained Visual Place Recognition Models
papers.summary: Visual place recognition (VPR) localises a camera by retrieving similar geo-tagged images, and current foundation-model VPR models are accurate across cities, seasons and illumination, but not robust to adversarial perturbations: under a white-box attack on the ranking at an imperceptible budget of 1/255, SuperVLAD and BoQ keep at most 0.2% top-1 recall (R@1) on four benchmarks. We propose anchored rank-adversarial fine-tuning (ARAFT), which fine-tunes a released model with a listwise rank loss on each adversarial query's hardest positive and an anchor to the clean descriptor of the frozen pretrained model. Checkpoints are selected under a clean-accuracy budget fixed in advance, and the full trade-off is reported. Within five validation R@1 points of clean cost, plain adversarial training has no admissible checkpoint, whereas ARAFT raises robust R@1 from zero to 47.3 on SuperVLAD and 55.3 on BoQ; plain adversarial training exceeds this only at about three times the clean cost. Against unbudgeted plain adversarial training on the test sets, ARAFT matches its robust R@1 at 2/255 with about ten more clean R@1 points. At 4/255, plain adversarial training is 6-9 robust R@1 points ahead, while ARAFT still keeps its ten-point clean advantage. Developed on SuperVLAD, ARAFT transfers to BoQ without re-tuning, and its robustness holds against stronger optimisers, with no sign of gradient masking.

papers.title: The Critical Cauchy Boundary for Gibbs Partitions
papers.summary: We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.

papers.title: Crossover duality for the quantum long-range Ising chain: perturbation theory around the short-range endpoint and a DMRG test
papers.summary: We propose a weakly coupled description of the long-range transverse-field Ising chain near its short-range crossover at $s_*=7/4$, where the couplings decay as $r^{-1-s}$. The Ising conformal field theory is coupled to an instantaneous Gaussian field through $σχ$, extending the classical long-range Ising duality to quantum chains. The equal-time interaction generates a stress-tensor deformation that causes the velocity to run and renormalizes the dynamical critical exponent $z$. Conformal perturbation theory gives $z=1-0.720\,δ+O(δ^2)$, $1/ν=(1+z)/2+O(δ^2)$, and $ω=δ+O(δ^2)$, with $δ=s_*-s$. DMRG calculations on periodic chains of up to $128$ sites provide a consistency test using theoretical inputs for $1/ν$ and $ω$. After accounting for slow finite-size corrections, static and dynamical estimates of $z$ agree, supporting the crossover expansion at $s=1.5$ and a two-sided Padé interpolation at $s=1$, $1.25$, and $1.5$.

papers.title: Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation
papers.summary: Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $λ_c$ from the classical value $2πr_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $λ_c<2πr_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $λ_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.

papers.title: Lagrangian Irreversibility in Stratified Turbulence
papers.summary: Stable stratification reorganizes turbulence, suppressing vertical motion and altering the balance between vortical and strain-dominated flow structures. How these changes affect the temporal asymmetry of kinetic-energy exchange along fluid-particle trajectories remains incompletely understood. Using direct numerical simulations of homogeneous Boussinesq turbulence, we investigate Lagrangian power statistics across four local velocity-gradient topology classes and three nonzero stratification strengths, with an unstratified reference case. With increasing stratification, the global power variance decreases while the standardized skewness becomes more negative, indicating enhanced asymmetry despite weaker fluctuations. Conditioning on local topology reveals distinct responses: axial-strain-dominated regions exhibit the most negative total-power skewness at all stratification strengths, whereas biaxial-strain-dominated regions change sign from positive to negative under stratification. Horizontal and vertical component powers also respond differently, revealing directional dependence. Among the dynamical contributions to power, the pressure contribution, nearly symmetric in the unstratified case, becomes more negatively skewed with increasing stratification. Energy-conditioned pressure statistics further indicate altered pressure-mediated energy redistribution. Finally, tracer persistence-time distributions exhibit exponential tails, with time scales that differ across topology classes and respond differently to stratification. Increasing stratification is thus accompanied by three concurrent changes: enhanced asymmetry of Lagrangian power, modified energy redistribution by pressure, and altered temporal sampling of local flow structures by tracers. These co-occurring signatures characterize the response to stratification, though their causal relations remain to be established.

papers.title: From Z to all: cyclic sum rules for thermal CFT partition functions
papers.summary: The high-temperature expansion of twisted $S^{d-1}\times S^1$ partition functions of CFT$_d$, $d = 2κ$, has recently been shown to obey an infinite tower of universal constraints. We determine these constraints explicitly and demonstrate that they can be packaged into a single equation involving a large conformal diffeomorphism isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_{κ+1}$, which cyclically permutes the thermal circle and the rotation angles. Our equation asserts that the $\mathbb{Z}_{κ+1}$-invariant part of $\ln Z/β$ is a constant fixed by the a-anomaly. Our derivation assumes CP-invariance and locality of the thermal effective action, whose structure we constrain using an algebraic formalism starting from embedding space.
papers.comment: 40 pages: 8 pages main Letter (including references), 2 pages appendices, and 30 pages Supplemental Material; 5 figures

papers.title: YANAMI: A Large-Scale Multimodal Dataset and Benchmark for Multiturn Stateful Interaction
papers.summary: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) integrate visual understanding, generation, and editing within a single unified framework. However, existing unified multimodal datasets and benchmarks remain dominated by single-turn tasks. Even in recent multi-turn datasets, many turns can be solved independently without tracking information across turns. Consequently, they provide limited supervision and evaluation for multimodal stateful interaction, which requires models to understand, maintain, update, and faithfully realize evolving dialogue states across turns. To address this gap, we introduce YANAMI, the first large-scale multimodal dialogue dataset and benchmark for stateful interaction, comprising YANAMI-400K and YANAMI-Bench. YANAMI-400K contains 400K multi-turn multimodal dialogues, with more than 2M images and 2.6M dialogue turns. The dialogues span four representative scenarios: Multi-Image Fusion, Image Editing, World Modeling, and Visual Reasoning, and require models to continuously track, preserve, and revise evolving multimodal dialogue states across turns. YANAMI-Bench comprises 400 multi-turn dialogues for systematically evaluating multimodal stateful interaction. It jointly evaluates Dialogue State Understanding and Visual Realization, characterizing the gap between models' ability to understand evolving dialogue states and their ability to faithfully realize them in visual outputs. Experiments show that fine-tuning BAGEL on YANAMI-400K improves image editing, generation, and multimodal stateful interaction by 10.3%, 2.0%, and 13.23%, respectively, while preserving its general visual understanding capabilities. Evaluations on YANAMI-Bench further reveal that existing UMMs still struggle to maintain, update, and visually realize evolving multimodal dialogue states.

papers.title: Möbius: A Unified Motion-Language Model Bridging Understanding and Generation
papers.summary: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. On HumanML3D, Möbius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data further demonstrates that our framework is both effective and scalable.

papers.title: Beyond Accuracy: What Language-Subspace Interventions Capture, Remove, and Improve
papers.summary: Language-subspace interventions aim to improve multilingual reasoning by suppressing language-related components in mid-layer activations. Using MATH and MGSM across four open-weight LLMs, we ask three questions: do estimated language subspaces capture translation-associated variation? Does projecting them out remove language information? And do they improve accuracy without compromising response language? For the first question, we build subspaces using the existing Mean-SVD construction and our DiffPCA. Both capture substantial translation-associated variation and show similar patterns across model depth. For the second, we project out each subspace and train linear probes to classify language from the projected activations. The probes still identify language almost perfectly, showing that neither subspace exhaustively captures language information. For the third, we evaluate several intervention configurations on Qwen2.5-7B, by varying subspace creation methods and intervention operators. We find that the intervention that most improves MGSM accuracy sacrifices response-language fidelity, with only one intervention improving joint accuracy--answers that are correct and in the target language--slightly, by 1.60 points. Interestingly, subtle changes in the prompt alone can reproduce the accuracy gains albeit with significant damage to language fidelity. We argue that causal interventions must be judged on more than accuracy, to fully account for language substitution trade-offs.

papers.title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity
papers.summary: Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage when calibration and test points are exchangeable, but exchangeability can fail when deployment changes the data distribution. We study conformal prediction in performative settings, where the deployed predictor affects the data distribution, and seek prediction sets valid at performative equilibrium: coverage must hold under $D(f^\star)$ for a performatively stable predictor $f^\star$. Under total-variation $L$-sensitivity of the distribution map, we prove a phase transition at $L=1$. If $L \ge 1$, no finite-sample procedure can uniformly guarantee both equilibrium-valid coverage and nontrivial prediction sets. If $L<1$, the minimax excess miscoverage over informative procedures is $\widetildeΩ(1/((1-L)\sqrt{n}))$, implying a sample-complexity inflation of order $1/(1-L)^2$ for fixed excess miscoverage. Our main technical tool is a transfer theorem: any procedure returning a predictor within $\varepsilon$ of equilibrium yields equilibrium-valid coverage up to an additive $L\varepsilon$ term after split-conformal calibration. We instantiate the theorem with two retraining algorithms: a model-free method for discretizable classes and a parametric tail-averaged method that matches the $n$- and $L$-dependence of this rate up to logarithmic factors. Experiments, including semi-synthetic credit scoring, demonstrate the predicted threshold behavior and scaling laws.

papers.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
papers.summary: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

papers.title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
papers.summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.

papers.title: A detailed star formation history of the distant Milky Way satellite Canes Venatici I: An old dwarf spheroidal forming most of its stars after reionisation
papers.summary: Canes Venatici I (CVnI) is a distant Milky Way (MW) dwarf spheroidal (dSph) satellite. To date, there is no consensus on its evolution and the properties of its stellar population. This work is aimed at obtaining an accurate picture of the star formation history (SFH) and metallicity distribution of CVnI to reconstruct its evolution in detail, as well as to infer the possible effects of internal and external feedback. We used archival HST/ACS observations to obtain the deepest colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) to date, reaching $\sim$2 mag below the old main sequence turn-off. We derived the SFH and metallicity distribution of CVnI using a state-of-the-art CMD-fitting technique. We found that the SFH is dominated by a single star formation period, which peaked around 11.8 Gyr ago, well after the reionisation epoch, and remained active until $\sim$10.4 Gyr ago. The galaxy's global metallicity, [Z/H], ranges from -2.4 to -1.5 dex. Interestingly, while its star population is old and metal-poor, compared to other MW satellites of a similar size and luminosity that formed most of their stars in a single burst, CVnI experienced a delayed star formation period. We carried out an exhaustive set of tests with synthetic and real populations to ensure the reliability of these results. We suggest that the evolution of CVnI could have been regulated by its mass accretion history. The galaxy would have evolved above (but still close to) a theoretic redshift-dependent critical mass above which it is possible to maintain star formation. The combined effect of SN feedback would have made CVnI's halo mass subcritical at z$\approx$2, definitively quenching its star formation. We cannot rule out the possible influence of gravitational interaction of CVnI with the MW at early ages, as hinted at by the most recent calculations of its orbit.

papers.title: Universal dynamics of quantum phase transitions with fractional long-range interactions
papers.summary: The complete statistical characterization of defects generated in a quantum phase transition has mostly been studied in exactly solvable models, and remains little explored in nonintegrable systems such as long-range interacting spin chains. We characterize the full defect counting statistics in a nonintegrable long-range spin chain, the fractional Ising model, by time-dependent variational-principle simulations within the matrix-product-state and matrix-product-operator formalism. Fractional interactions capture emergent multiscale correlations and long-range effects in nature, governed by the order of the underlying fractional derivative. Such couplings can be approximated on existing quantum simulation platforms, where the full defect statistics can be measured. The defect number cumulants follow power laws in the driving time, with exponents that vary continuously with the fractional order. At low fractional order, deep in the long-range regime, the mean defect number decays more slowly than predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM), while at intermediate order the KZM holds with the numerically extracted many-body critical exponents. At large fractional order, the exactly solvable free-fermion limit of the model becomes progressively more accurate towards the short-range limit. We derive exact bounds on the kink-number cumulants and on the kink-kink correlations, implying an exact Gaussian limiting distribution for large system sizes. In the many-body simulations, however, kinks are more correlated, consistent with the confinement of domain walls, and these bounds are violated in the long-range regime, also in the bulk of the chain. Nevertheless, the kink distribution still approaches a Gaussian for large defect numbers, with proportionality partially broken between the cumulants.
papers.comment: 28 pages, 13 pages main text, 12 pages appendices, 3 pages bibliography, 15 figures, 8 figures in the main text, 7 figures in the appendices

papers.title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
papers.summary: Evaluating whether a large language model (LLM) genuinely knows a concept remains a fundamental problem, since behavioral metrics can be fooled by suppression: a model that refuses to answer may still harbor recoverable knowledge. The framework measures the geometric coherence of \textit{anon-vectors}, the differences in hidden states between a concept-specific query and its anonymized paraphrase, and shows that genuine knowledge forms a tight, low-entropy cluster while ignorance forces geometric fragmentation. Across ten instruction-tuned LLMs from three model families, all fragmentation metrics reliably separate known from unknown concepts, and post-unlearning, fragmentation geometry correlates with adversarial recovery across four attack types and five unlearning algorithms, though the direction of that relationship is shown to depend on attack methodology. Furthermore, a layer-resolved analysis reveals that different adversarial mechanisms exploit this geometry at varying depths, with high attack-specific correlations that are invisible to behavioral evaluation. Together, these results constitute a single-phase, attack-free proxy for unlearning robustness that captures aspects of parametric knowledge inaccessible to output-level metrics. A reference implementation is available at https://github.com/AdarPeleg/geometry-of-ignorance

papers.title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
papers.summary: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.

papers.title: Effective Hamiltonians and non-Hermitian physics
papers.summary: Every realistic quantum system is coupled to an environment. Including the environment restores a closed, Hermitian description, but at the cost of an intractably large Hilbert space. The Feshbach--Löwdin projection eliminates the unwanted degrees of freedom exactly, yielding an effective Hamiltonian $H_{\rm eff}$ on the relevant subspace alone---which \new{generically becomes non-Hermitian when the eliminated subspace contains an energetically accessible continuum and outgoing boundary conditions are imposed}. We illustrate this through a minimal model: a particle in a box with a delta barrier at its center. Direct elimination of one half-well reduces all information about the discarded sector to a single \new{boundary parameter} $β$; the same result is then rederived via the Green's function and Dyson equation, offering a pedagogical illustration of how boundary data enter the Green's-function formalism and relating $β$ to a self-energy term. Whether $β$ is real or complex determines whether $H_{\rm eff}$ is Hermitian or not, and the full range of behavior---from Hermitian dynamics through finite-width resonances to the counterintuitive quantum Zeno effect---follows from this single parameter.

papers.title: On the van der Corput property for cubes
papers.summary: We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.

papers.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Naive on-policy RL is often bottlenecked by the capabilities of the base model --- insufficient coverage can result in an inability to learn from certain rewards. At the same time, rewards in modern post-training systems often come from rich textual sources, e.g. judge models with a rubric of criteria. Can we utilize such structures to provide a rich directional signal that enables improving on otherwise difficult to optimize rewards? In this work, we examine a framework we refer to as targeted guidance that learns from per-turn textual feedback via an on-policy self-distillation objective. Our focus is not only on directly improving hard-to-optimize behaviors, but on how to do so throughout the training process without degrading baseline RL performance. Over a range of settings across an agentic multi-turn software engineering environment, we find success by combining targeted self-distillation with a per-criteria RL reward, and by limiting feedback to turns where the policy specifically fails. We further examine the design choices that lead to stable entropy and reduce oscillatory behavior throughout training.

papers.title: Gaussian Partitioning for Reliable Learning of Multi-Index Models
papers.summary: We introduce Gaussian partitioning, an algorithmic primitive for distributions smooth with respect to a Gaussian. It partitions space into polyhedral regions so that almost all mass lies in thin strips restricting a few orthogonal directions. Within each strip, the conditional distribution approximately matches low-degree Gaussian moments in the unrestricted directions. Our construction builds on logconcave partitioning of Diakonikolas, Kane, and Ma (FOCS 2026). Under input marginals smooth with respect to the standard Gaussian, we obtain agnostic learners with error $(1+c)\mathrm{opt}+ε$ for broad classes of Boolean multi-index models, including functions of halfspaces, low-dimensional convex concepts, and low-dimensional polynomial threshold functions. For functions of $k$ halfspaces, both agnostic and testable agnostic learners achieve this error with dimension dependence $d^{\mathrm{poly}(k/c)}$, improving the previous exponential dependence on $k/c$ in the agnostic exponent. For learning from positive examples with imperfect unlabeled data (PUI), we give algorithms and Statistical Query (SQ) lower bounds that qualitatively characterize complexity through Gaussian moment matching. For fixed smoothness and positive-mass parameters, we learn intersections of $k$ halfspaces with dimension dependence $d^{O(\log(k/ε))}$ and matching SQ lower bounds, improving the previous $d^{\mathrm{poly}(1/ε)}$ upper bound even for one halfspace. A general reduction from agnostic reliable learning to PUI yields negative reliable learners for these intersections with the same dimension dependence, for fixed smoothness. Finally, for PQ learning and testable learning with distribution shift, we prove qualitatively optimal SQ lower bounds of $d^{Ω(1/ε^2)}$, even for intersections of two halfspaces with Gaussian training data and arbitrary test distributions.

papers.title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
papers.summary: Multimodal web agents have shown promising capabilities for interacting with websites through graphical user interfaces (GUIs), yet realistic web tasks often require long-horizon, multi-step planning that remains challenging for monolithic policies. Such agents must jointly infer high-level plans, navigate through intermediate states, track progress over extended interaction histories, and execute visually grounded actions. Although prior work has explored modular multi-agent systems with a separate planner, the planner is typically not updated jointly with the actor. We investigate whether explicitly separating and jointly training planning and execution provides a stronger inductive bias for long-horizon web navigation. We introduce JHiMA-WebRL, a joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for web agents that couples a task decomposer with an actor. To train the decomposer, we use a strong teacher model to construct structured subtask supervision from multimodal GUI trajectories, and use these annotations to fine-tune both the decomposer and the subtask-conditioned actor. We then extend Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to jointly optimize the decomposer and actor in the interactive WebArena environment through hierarchical rollout grouping and role-specific advantages. On WebArena-Lite-v2, JHiMA-WebRL-14B, consisting of a 7B actor and a 7B decomposer, achieves an average success rate of 37.2%, compared with 24% for a ScaleCUA-32B agent that we fine-tune with RL on the same training tasks and evaluate under the same protocol. Ablations show that jointly updating the decomposer during RL outperforms updating the actor alone. These results suggest that jointly learned role factorization with smaller models can be a competitive alternative to scaling monolithic agents for long-horizon web tasks.

papers.title: Global Existence for a Drift-Diffusion Model of Electrical Discharge in MEMS
papers.summary: We study a coupled elliptic-parabolic system modelling electrical discharge in a micro-electro-mechanical (MEMS) capacitor: a Poisson equation for the electrostatic potential, coupled to drift-diffusion equations for the ion and electron densities with a Townsend ionization source whose rate per electron grows linearly in the electric field. Gimperlein, He and Lacey proved local well-posedness and left open whether the densities blow up in finite time. We first prove a continuation criterion in a weak norm: a finite-time singularity forces the space charge to be unbounded in H^1_D, the dual of the space of H^1 functions vanishing on the electrodes, so blow-up cannot be quasi-neutral. We then exclude it altogether when the two diffusivities coincide and the vacuum field is bounded: the weak solution is then global in time. To our knowledge this is the first global existence result without smallness assumptions for a drift-diffusion-Poisson model of gas discharge whose ionization rate is unbounded in the field. The proof uses the electrostatic energy and the number of carriers in place of the usual free energy: the ionization source cancels in the energy balance, the Joule heating is dissipative, and the two quantities close through a linear Gronwall inequality. Numerical experiments on a discharge in a micrometre gap, with the Townsend constants and the mobilities of air, provide evidence for the extension to unequal diffusivities and bear on the existence of a breakdown threshold.

papers.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erdős--Sós $(9,6)$-problem
papers.summary: Let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. It has long been conjectured that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, settling the first unsolved case of the conjecture.

papers.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice
papers.summary: De novo peptide sequencing has moved from dynamic programming over hand-designed or generative scores to large transformers that learn the task end to end. We present NovoCRF, a conditional random field (CRF) whose states are prefix masses, so that its paths are exactly the peptides within +/-0.06 Da of the precursor mass. A small network scores each edge from physics-derived ion-match features and is trained with its scores globally normalized over all mass-feasible peptides. To our knowledge, NovoCRF is the first de novo method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible peptides. Our software has three modules, each with exactly one job: a precursor mass finder recovers the accurate precursor mass from MS1, the CRF finds the peptides that fit the precursor mass by exact k-best decoding, and two BiGRU rerankers add sequence context and internal-fragment evidence. The model has 310k parameters and trains in about 17 GPU-hours. On seven held-out data-dependent acquisition datasets published in 2026 (126,262 labeled spectra), NovoCRF's mean peptide recall is 42.4%, against 39.1% for Casanovo v5 with five beams, and its amino-acid recall 64.0% against 53.1%, at 1,746 spectra/s on 18 CPU threads, 55x Casanovo's throughput on a GPU. Split by fragment evidence, NovoCRF leads on labels with up to three peptide bonds without a b or y ion, and Casanovo only beyond. NovoCRF can also search modifications it was never trained on at their exact mass: it finds 32.1% of the hydroxyproline peptides of a lion bone sample.

papers.title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
papers.summary: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

papers.title: Universality in Anomalous Diffusion: Power Laws and Faster-Decaying Tails
papers.summary: Strong anomalous diffusion is often characterized by a piecewise-linear spectrum of the moments of displacement. The spectrum is characterized by the slopes $θ$ and $ζ$ for small and large moments, respectively, and by the crossover moment $q_c$ at which the slope changes. The exponents $θ$ and $ζ$ characterize the asymptotic scaling of the bulk and of the tails of the probability distribution function of displacements, respectively. Here, we adopt asymptotic theory to match the behaviors at intermediate scales. The resulting constraint explains how distributions with algebraic tails imply strong anomalous diffusion, and it relates $q_c$ to the corresponding power law. Our theory provides universal hyper-scaling relations between the exponents characterizing strong anomalous diffusion, and it yields explicit expressions for the leading-order corrections to the asymptotic power-law behavior of the moments of displacement. We also characterize finite-time corrections and propose a robust distribution-based method to estimate $θ$, $ζ$, and $q_c$. The findings are supported by numerical and analytical results for three paradigmatic models exhibiting strong anomalous diffusion. Finally, we show that power-law tails are not only sufficient but also necessary for this scenario: with a Gaussian, or generally fast-decaying, bulk and exponentially rare ballistic excursions, the spectrum of moments is single-linear, and the crossover to the apparent second branch drifts with the observation time. When the bulk is fast decaying and the tail is a power law, strong anomalous diffusion is still present, but the hyper-scaling relations among the exponents are violated.

papers.title: Weak solutions to granular medium equations via stochastic particle approximations
papers.summary: We establish weak existence for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations associated with granular medium equations with porous medium diffusion, for m>1 in arbitrary dimension. The result covers a class of nonconvex potentials with locally Lipschitz gradients of polynomial growth. Our particle approximation generates nonlinear diffusion through density-dependent noise and allows initial densities with finite Boltzmann entropy but infinite internal energy.

papers.title: Going Deeper With Memories
papers.summary: Byte level language models avoid tokenizer dependence and provide universal coverage, but processing every byte at full resolution is expensive. We introduce DeepMem, a causal multiscale architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation. A learned invertible subband transform constructs a hierarchy of shorter sequences, while a lossless carrier and explicit detail sidebands preserve byte identity. Fast weight memory blocks operate along the encoder, with iterative shared state computation at the compressed bottleneck, while an attention based super resolution decoder restores byte resolution representations. DeepMem achieves stronger language modeling performance than a matched byte level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu and PG19, and obtains the best macro average performance across the evaluated FLORES languages. It also improves PIQA accuracy while remaining competitive on code modeling, multiple choice reasoning, and byte level corruption robustness. Bottleneck refinement requires approximately $7{,}600\times$ fewer counted FLOPs than equivalent full resolution reasoning, while maintaining competitive evaluation throughput.
